newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: New OECD guidelines set for trade-tied aid credits.
newsitem.headline: New OECD guidelines set for trade-tied aid credits.

text.p: Members countries of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) have agreed new guidelines for export-linked aid packages, the Swiss government said on Thursday.

The measures, adopted by the OECD's 22-member Export Credit Arrangement, are designed to prevent trade-linked aid programmes from distorting competition and commerce by offering credits that can be used only to finance exports from donor countries.

"The guidelines contain concrete indications for determining the commercial viability for projects in specific sectors such as energy production, telecommunications, transport and industry," the Federal Office for International Economics said.
"They are complemented by a checklist for producing feasibility studies as well as directions for project definitions and cash flow calculations," it said in a statement.
Switzerland chaired the talks, which were based on principles first agreed in Helsinki in 1992.
